edges.description: Lethal infection in interferon-deficient mice reproduces the uncontrolled high-titre replication that type I interferon normally restricts.
edges.limitations: Disease requires genetic or antibody-mediated ablation of type I interferon signalling; immunocompetent wild-type mice resist lethal infection, so the model cannot address how intact innate immunity controls CCHFV and biases toward immune-evasion questions.

edges.description: Infected interferon-deficient mice develop the liver pathology seen in fatal human disease, with hepatocytes as targets of infection.

This is the CCHF-specific substitution at the module's shared high-viremia node.
